goal: Add two new WARN-severity mechanical checks to scripts/spec-lint.mjs, extending A1's frozen lintSpec shape without redefining it. (a) validation_lane: read the project's `## validate` fenced block for its `full:` lane and warn when a spec's validation_commands entry is that full-suite command verbatim (the full suite runs once at ship, never per coder). (b) test_ownership: warn when acceptance_criteria mentions test coverage but names no owner — no test file in files_in_scope and no literal `dev-team:test-engineer` — mechanizing the completeness rule already written into handover-spec.md's checklist. Both checks are advisory (warn, never fail): they must not change any exit code, and the existing four checks' severity, wording, and ordering are untouched. The test file gains positive AND negative pins for each new check per its own VACUITY LENS convention, and the CHECK-NAME MANIFEST test grows from four names to six.

NOTE ON PATHS BELOW: fixture paths are written with a leading `@` (e.g. @tests/foo.py) so spec-lint's own bare-mention pass ignores them — they name files inside the throwaway tmpdir fixture, not files in this repo. Strip the `@` when you write code.

1. WHERE THE NEW CALLS GO — scripts/spec-lint.mjs:409-412, the bottom of lintSpec:
```
  checkSchema(spec)
  checkFilesInScope(spec, resolvedRoot)
  checkDiscoveryRefs(spec, resolvedRoot)
  checkValidationCommands(spec, resolvedRoot)

  return { ok: failures.length === 0, failures, warnings }
```
Append `checkValidationLane(spec, resolvedRoot)` then `checkTestOwnership(spec)` before the return. Both are declared INSIDE lintSpec (they need the closure-scoped `warn`), exactly like the existing four. Order is load-bearing: warnings are appended in call order and existing tests index `r.warnings[0]`.

2. PATTERN TO MIRROR — the tokenization checkValidationLane must REUSE (scripts/spec-lint.mjs:387-395):
```
    for (const cmd of spec.validation_commands) {
      // Non-string entries are already reported by checkSchema.
      if (typeof cmd !== 'string') continue
      const tokens = cmd.trim().split(/\s+/).filter((t) => !/^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=/.test(t))
      if (!tokens.length) {
        fail('validation_commands', `empty command: ${JSON.stringify(cmd)}`)
        continue
      }
```
checkValidationLane uses that same `tokens` expression and compares `tokens.join(' ')` to the config value. Do not re-derive it.

3. PATTERN TO MIRROR — the module-level, root-relative, never-throws reader (scripts/spec-lint.mjs:197-205):
```
function packageScripts(root) {
  const p = join(root, 'package.json')
  if (!existsSync(p)) return null
  try {
    return JSON.parse(readFileSync(p, 'utf8')).scripts || {}
  } catch {
    return null
  }
}
```
`readValidateFullCommand(root)` sits beside it with the same shape, but wraps `readFileSync` in a bare try/catch with NO existsSync pre-check — the catch already covers ENOENT/EISDIR/EACCES, and existsSync-then-read is the TOCTOU shape conventions.md 2026-08-02 warns about. It joins `root` with '.claude', 'dev-team', 'config.md'. **Do NOT memoize it** — unlike loadSchema/loadNoiseGlobs (one packaged asset, memoized safely from `import.meta.url`), this is per-root instance data, and a memoized value would leak across two lintSpec calls with different roots in one process, exactly what the CROSS-CONTAMINATION test at test/spec-lint.test.mjs:113 exists to prevent.

4. THE CONFIG SHAPE it parses — .claude/dev-team/config.md in this repo, section `## validate`:
```
## validate

```
fast: node --test
full: node --test
```
```
Parse: find `/^##\s+validate\s*$/m`; slice from there to the next `/^##\s/m` heading (or EOF); find the FIRST fenced block in that slice; find `/^\s*full:\s*(.+)$/m` inside the block's content; return the value `.trim()`, or null if empty. Any step failing returns null. Deliberate decisions to encode as comments: (i) first `full:` wins on a duplicate — this reader is advisory, so ambiguity degrades to the first value rather than refusing, the opposite of `readExecutionMode`'s refuse-on-ambiguity (scripts/cmux/dispatch.mjs:88), which gates a real dispatch; (ii) the config-side value is compared trimmed only, never re-tokenized, so odd internal whitespace in config.md yields a false NEGATIVE (silence) rather than a false positive — the safe direction for an advisory check.

5. THE TWO DIAGNOSTIC STRINGS (tests pin distinctive substrings of these, not the whole string):
- `warn('validation_lane', `"${cmd}" matches config.validate.full verbatim — the full suite runs once at /dev-team:ship, not per coder; use the scoped fast lane narrowed to files_in_scope instead`)`
- `warn('test_ownership', 'acceptance_criteria mentions test coverage but no owner is named (no test file in files_in_scope, and dev-team:test-engineer not named) — see handover-spec.md's completeness checklist')`
Pin them from the tests with /matches config\.validate\.full/ and /no owner is named/.

6. checkTestOwnership ALGORITHM (all three conditions must hold before warning; emit at most ONE diagnostic per spec):
- mention: for each string criterion, first strip quoted spans — `c.replace(/"[^"]*"|`[^`]*`/g, ' ')` (an unpaired quote strips nothing, which is correct) — then test the remainder against `/\b(test|tests|testing|coverage|tested)\b/i`.
- hasTestFile: any string entry of files_in_scope matching this set (case-insensitive; each verified against the AC-7 matrix): `/(^|\/)(tests?|__tests__)\//`, `/(^|\/)[^/]*\.(test|spec)\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$/`, `/(^|\/)test_[^/]*\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$/`, `/(^|\/)[^/]*_test\.[A-Za-z0-9]+$/`. The anchored `(^|\/)` is what keeps `@contest/foo.js` and `@src/api/latest.ts` out.
- namesGateOwner: any criterion's FULL, UNSTRIPPED text `.includes('dev-team:test-engineer')` — unstripped deliberately, because criteria conventionally wrap that token in backticks and the stripping pass would erase it.
Signature note: I specified `checkTestOwnership(spec)` — no `root` parameter (the issue text said `(spec, root)`); the check touches no filesystem, and an unused parameter would invite a future reader to assume a root dependency that does not exist. If you disagree, keep `(spec, root)` and comment that root is intentionally unused — but do not read the filesystem in it.

8. WHY WARN AND NOT FAIL — the existing severity convention: FAIL is reserved for unambiguous mechanical facts (missing path with missing parent, unresolvable npm script, binary not on PATH); string/keyword heuristics warn (the noise-glob match at scripts/spec-lint.mjs:249-252 is the precedent). It also matters doctrinally: orchestration.md's Handover Spec section classifies a missing coverage owner as a SEMANTIC-lint bounce, 'not a mechanical one' — a WARN keeps the decision at the orchestrator's eyeball layer while surfacing the fact mechanically, whereas a FAIL would contradict shipped doctrine. Do not change that sentence; it is out of scope.

9. PRODUCTION EFFECT WORTH KNOWING: this repo's own `full:` lane is `node --test`, so after this change any spec authored here whose validation_commands is exactly `node --test` will warn. That is the intended behavior, and it is why this spec's own commands are file-scoped.
